title: Section normalization of finite scalar restriction and direct image
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, schemes X,Y, a morphism f:X→Y and n≥0. Use the actual finiteScalarRestrictionDirect(f,n) of [lem-sf-integral-finite-scalar-pull-ordinary]. For every finite-coefficient module N on X, every object V of Y.ProEt, and every x in N evaluated at the base change of V along f, the underlying section of finiteScalarRestrictionDirect(f,n).hom_N at V sends x to x, up to heterogeneous equality accounting for the equality transport in finiteDirectImage_eq. No nonzero module or nonempty-scheme hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: The scalar/pullback comparison on a flat-term K-flat representative in the finite-evaluation argument; Stacks Tags 07A6, 06YY and 0D6E.

proof.text: The ringed restriction/direct-image comparison is identity on sections by the predicate that uniquely defines it. The preceding finiteDirectImage_eq contributes equality transport only. Equality induction on the functor equality shows that whiskering the equality isomorphism preserves the heterogeneous identity of sections. Compose these heterogeneous equalities. This argument has no nonzero-module or positive-exponent restriction beyond n+1.
